summary: Groundwork for child chats on other machines (design 2026-10-29): the VM backend lifecycle and token. This part is not gated by a flag. the remote bootstrap starts the headless backend and the managed code-server detached (setsid nohup, output in ~/.switchboard-server/server.log), so a tunnel drop, a desktop sleep or a quit no longer ends the sessions on the VM. Each connect reuses a live backend when its pid is still ours, it was started from the installed version (server.version equals version) and its HTTP listener answers within 3 s; otherwise it reaps the backend and code-server as before and starts fresh ones. The ssh session waits on the backend pid, so the tunnel ends when the server dies. The backend now always runs with a token: the bootstrap keeps it 0600 in ~/.switchboard-server/token and prints it once on the ssh channel; the desktop reads it from the tunnel output (never logged), keeps it in memory, sends it in the health probe and gives it to the renderer through a desktop-only IPC call (not the backend host, which also serves phones). The renderer sends it in an auth frame; WsHost accepts the server token in an auth frame with the same scopes as the URL token. On reuse, a code-server that does not answer on its port is reaped and started again. The bootstrap sets 0600 on an existing token file and exits when it cannot create a token. Scope hub and the hub-remote skeleton (PR 2), behind the staged flag hub_remote_children (HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN_ENABLED in src/shared/hub.ts, false; SB_HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN=1 or the backend setting labs.hub_remote_children turns it on, and only while hub_children is on). A new DeviceScope hub opens the hub-remote:* channels and events and nothing else; every other channel now needs chat, which every phone, device session, server token and the IAP TCP host already holds (a stored device row without chat gets it, and hub is dropped from any device credential). Only the server token grants hub: its auth frame may carry scopes, and the backend grants the asked scopes the token holds (hub when it holds admin) or refuses the auth. The capability hub_remote_child_v1 is advertised. hub-remote:describe answers on the desktop and the headless server, with the flag off too: flag state, OS, architecture, backend version, agents that run there with their enabled accounts and catalog models, up to 200 projects with branch and fetch remote URLs (git with a 5 s timeout, one bad repository does not fail the answer), free disk under ~/projects or home, open children and run slots per account. It holds no host name, cloud project, zone or user name. The events hub-remote:outbox and hub-remote:children-changed are declared without an emitter. The desktop hub client and list_machines (PR 3), behind hub_remote_children: RemoteHubClients in the desktop main process opens one WebSocket client per connected machine from the ConnectionManager status (tunnel URL and backend token, ?auth=frame, auth frame scopes hub), accepts only an authed of exactly hub and a ready with hub_remote_child_v1 (otherwise it closes and the machine reads 'update the backend on <name>'), closes on disconnect, delete and quit, refuses a call to a machine that is not connected at once and times a call out after 20 s, with a hub.remote-call perf line per call. It reads hub-remote:describe on every connect and at most every 60 s on demand, keeps an offline machine's last answer with its age and caches no failure. A parent chat that is not an open child, on the desktop's own backend (not SWITCHBOARD_REMOTE), gets the read-only tool list_machines and one more instruction line while the flag is on: this desktop first, then each saved machine with id, the user's name for it, transport, status, OS and architecture, agents with accounts and models, checkouts whose git remote matches the chat project's (https, ssh and scp forms compare as one key), free disk, open children, free run slots, and a line when the flag is off there or the backend needs an update. It never writes a host name, ssh alias, cloud project, zone or user name. With the flag off no client opens and the tool and line are absent. machine on start_children tasks, the batch card and propose checks (PR 4), behind hub_remote_children: a task may name a machine id from list_machines (type and length checked; local or absent is this machine), documented in the tool schema only where list_machines is offered. With the flag off, or from a parent on a VM, such a task is refused. Propose checks each remote task against the hub client's cached description (known, connected, no client problem, a fresh description, flagOn there, a login and the named account and model, a worktree location, a parent project with a git remote), uses a checkout there whose remote matches or plans a clone into ~/projects/<repo>, resolves the base to a commit a remote branch holds (the parent's upstream first; Switchboard does not push) and checks that machine's free disk against its own floor; the first problem refuses the batch, naming the task. The stored plan carries machine, remoteProjectPath, clonePlanned and fetch; a plan stored before reads as local. A batch with any remote child always opens the card, in every mode, with the machine per row, the clone note and one disk line per machine in the card and its plain text. Approval re-reads the machines; a machine that is gone, offline or lost the account fails only its own children, and every approved remote child ends as failed_start with a failed wake (starting there comes in a later version). Local children in the batch start as before.

desktop.followUpRelease: The release that turns hub_remote_children on by default (HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN_ENABLED true), after hub_children is on by default and children on another machine run end to end from the desktop on the beta channel.

reactNativeIos.reason: Phones never dial a VM's tunnelled backend; they reach the desktop only, or a VM's own TCP listener with the token the operator set, which this change does not touch. The hub scope is never granted to a phone: pairing and device grants cannot carry it, and every phone scope set holds chat, so no phone channel changes. The batch card reaches phones as the plain detail text only, which now names the machine per row; no phone code changes.

nativeAndroid.reason: Same as iOS: the Android app does not use the ssh bootstrap or the desktop's tunnel, and its IAP path to a VM's TCP listener is unchanged. Same for the hub scope: Android sessions hold chat and never hub. Android also shows the batch card's detail text only; it does not read tests/fixtures/hub-cases.json.

sharedBackendApi.followUpRelease: The release that turns hub_remote_children on by default (HUB_REMOTE_CHILDREN_ENABLED true), after hub_children is on by default and children on another machine run end to end from the desktop on the beta channel.

storageDataMigration.reason: No database or settings change. The VM gains two flat files under ~/.switchboard-server (token, 0600, and server.version); a missing server.version makes the first connect after the upgrade reap the old foreground server, as every connect did before. The hub scope adds no column or setting; a stored device session row is read with chat added when it lacks it and hub dropped, which never narrows what it could reach before. PR 4 adds optional fields to the stored hub_batches.plan_json and to the agent card's hubBatch view, with no migration: a plan or card stored before has none of them and reads as local.

npx vitest run tests/unit/hub-remote-propose.test.ts tests/unit/hub-rules.test.ts tests/unit/hub-start.test.ts --maxWorkers=2: machine parsing; every propose refusal (flag off, VM parent, unknown, offline, client problem, stale or missing description, flag off there, no login, unknown account or model, location project, no git remote, base not on a remote, remote disk); project matching across https, ssh and scp forms and the clone plan; the card forced in accept-edits, auto and full access when a row is remote and unchanged for local-only batches (fixture needsCard); hubBatchDetail text; at approval an offline machine fails only its children, a lost account fails its child, the rest end as a later version and the local child starts; a plan stored without machine fields starts as local; the schema documents machine only with list_machines.
notExercised: Phones: no change on that path.
PR 3: list_machines was not run against a real VM through an IAP or ssh tunnel, nor on a packaged build from existing user data; the hub client was exercised against an in-process WsHost only.
PR 4: the propose checks and the card were not run against a real VM, nor on a packaged build from existing user data; no remote child starts in this version.
